goals.title: Clean a candidate mask using morphology
goals.why: Distinguish closing gaps from opening isolated pixels.
explain: Binary closing can fill narrow gaps and join neighboring bright components.
Binary opening removes thin protrusions but may erase true small objects.
Structuring-element size must be predeclared relative to expected biological scale.

goals.why: Learn when watershed creates plausible but unvalidated object boundaries.
explain: Distance-transform watershed separates touching foreground when markers are credible.

An algorithmically separated component is not yet an annotated nucleus.

build_steps: Inspect all inputs and declare parameters before running.
Apply multiple chapter methods without mutating source arrays.
Report changed-input outcomes and excluded or ambiguous records.
Export the resulting source code and document non-calibrated limitations.

review.title: Diagnose border-exclusion failures
review.why: Reconstruct the method after a delay on a fresh input.
explain: Reproduce the key numerical decision from memory.
Check edge behavior and compare to a second input.
Do not equate remembered code with biological validation.

worked_example.predict: Predict the printed numerical result and one limitation before execution.

review.prediction_answer: Check the printed values against the chosen axis, units and algorithm; a computational check is not experimental validation.
walkthrough: Identify the source arrays, parameters and expected output before changing code.
Run the worked example and record which choice alters a candidate measurement.
Inspect one boundary input and distinguish a mask from validated biological identity.
investigate: Change one input value or ROI deliberately.
Inspect source data and a failure case rather than trusting a clean-looking overlay.
Record the scientific meaning of the output and its denominator.
review.debug_task: Diagnose one shape, threshold, indexing or data-provenance failure and explain how a changed input exposes it.
review.misconception: Numerically plausible image features are automatically true objects or independent biological replicates.
review.scientific_boundary: Examples are synthetic unless a credited Witz/HPA rendered PNG is explicitly decoded; no raw calibration or manually validated segmentation is implied.
